domains.name: Number Sense & Estimation
subtopics: Place value and magnitude
Read, compose and compare whole numbers and decimals by place value; use powers of ten to explain magnitude.
Compare 4,080 and 4,008 by examining the hundreds and tens places.
A common error is treating 0 as having no structural role; in 4,080 it preserves the tens place.
Estimate sums and products before calculating exactly; reject answers whose size is impossible.
Rounding and estimation
Round integers and decimals to stated place values and use estimation to predict reasonable answers.
Round 7,496 to the nearest hundred: 7,500 because the tens digit is 9.
When estimating 398×21, use 400×20=8,000 as a reasonableness benchmark.
Use compatible numbers, bounds and reverse checks to verify numerical answers.
Factors, multiples and primes
Identify factors, multiples, primes, composite numbers, common factors and common multiples.
For 36, factor pairs are 1×36, 2×18, 3×12 and 4×9.
A number divisible by 6 must be divisible by both 2 and 3.
Apply divisibility rules, prime factorisation, GCD and LCM in unfamiliar problems.
Mental calculation strategies
Choose efficient mental methods for addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and percentage calculations.
Use 25×16 as 100÷4×16=400 rather than repeated addition.
Watch for carrying and place-value errors when splitting numbers mentally.
Select a method, estimate first, calculate, then verify using an inverse operation.
Number properties and puzzles
Use parity, divisibility, remainders and numerical structure to solve non-routine problems.
If an integer is odd, adding another odd integer produces an even result.
A remainder must be smaller than the divisor; this gives an immediate validity check.
Combine parity and divisibility constraints to eliminate impossible cases before calculation.

domains.name: Fractions, Ratios & Proportion
subtopics: Equivalent fractions and simplification
Generate equivalent fractions, reduce fractions using common factors, and compare fractions reliably.
3/4 and 9/12 represent the same quantity because both simplify to 3/4.
Do not compare denominators alone; convert to common denominators or benchmark against 1/2 and 1.
Solve comparison and ordering problems involving mixed numbers and improper fractions.
Fraction operations
Add, subtract, multiply and divide fractions while explaining why each operation works.
For 2/3+1/6, rewrite 2/3 as 4/6, giving 5/6.
Division by a fraction asks how many groups of that size fit into the dividend.
Use inverse operations and magnitude estimates to detect impossible fraction results.
Ratios and equivalent ratios
Interpret ratios as comparisons and scale them without changing the underlying relationship.
A 2:3 ratio becomes 8:12 when both parts are multiplied by 4.
A ratio is not automatically a fraction of the whole; distinguish comparison from total share.
Solve missing-value, mixture and scale problems using tables, unit rates or equivalent ratios.
Proportion and scaling
Recognise proportional relationships and apply scale factors to quantities, diagrams and rates.
If 3 notebooks cost ₹90, the unit price is ₹30 and 7 cost ₹210 under the same rate.
A proportional relationship keeps the same multiplicative scale factor.
Test whether a relationship is truly proportional before applying cross-multiplication.
Percentages in context
Convert between fractions, decimals and percentages and apply percentage change to real situations.
15% of ₹800 is ₹120, so the discounted price is ₹680.
A 20% increase followed by a 20% decrease does not return to the starting value.
Solve discount, tax, comparison and percentage-change problems with explicit base quantities.

domains.name: Algebraic Reasoning
subtopics: Variables and expressions
Represent unknown quantities with variables and translate verbal descriptions into algebraic expressions.
Five more than x is x+5; five times x is 5x.
Do not confuse addition with multiplication when translating phrases.
Evaluate expressions for given values and explain the role of each term.
Simplifying expressions
Combine like terms and use distributive reasoning to simplify algebraic expressions.
3x+5x becomes 8x because both terms contain the same variable quantity.
2(x+3) means two groups of both x and 3, so it becomes 2x+6.
Check simplification by substituting a numerical value for x before and after.
Equations and unknowns
Solve one- and multi-step equations while preserving equality.
For 3x+5=20, subtract 5 then divide by 3 to obtain x=5.
Performing the same operation on both sides preserves equality.
Substitute the solution back into the original equation to verify it.
Inequalities and constraints
Interpret inequality symbols and solve simple constrained problems.
x>4 includes every number greater than 4, not 4 itself.
Boundary values determine whether an inequality is strict or inclusive.
Translate word constraints into inequalities and test candidate values.
Algebraic word problems
Build equations from real situations involving unknowns, rates, totals and comparisons.
If three equal notebooks and a ₹20 pen cost ₹140, represent the notebook price as x and solve 3x+20=140.
Identify the unknown and units before writing the equation.
Check the solution against the original story, including units and non-negative constraints.

subtopics.title: Angles and relationships
subtopics.teaching: Use straight-line, around-a-point, vertically opposite and triangle angle facts to determine unknown angles.
subtopics.worked_example: Angles on a straight line total 180°, so an angle of 127° leaves 53°.
subtopics.pitfall: Diagrams are not necessarily drawn to scale; use stated mathematical relationships.
subtopics.mastery: Combine multiple angle facts and verify the final angle against the geometry.

subtopics.title: Perimeter and area
subtopics.teaching: Calculate perimeter and area of standard and composite figures and distinguish the two measures.
subtopics.worked_example: An 8 cm by 5 cm rectangle has area 40 cm² and perimeter 26 cm.
subtopics.pitfall: Perimeter measures boundary length; area measures covered surface.
subtopics.mastery: Decompose composite figures and check units: cm for perimeter, cm² for area.

subtopics.title: Triangles and polygons
subtopics.teaching: Classify polygons and apply side and angle properties to solve problems.
subtopics.worked_example: An equilateral triangle has three equal sides and three 60° angles.
subtopics.pitfall: A quadrilateral has interior-angle sum 360°.
subtopics.mastery: Use known properties rather than visual appearance to justify classification.

subtopics.title: Volume and measurement
subtopics.teaching: Calculate volume and convert length, area and volume units consistently.
subtopics.worked_example: A 4×3×2 cm cuboid has volume 24 cm³.
subtopics.pitfall: Area uses squared units and volume uses cubed units.
subtopics.mastery: Convert units before combining quantities and check dimensional consistency.

subtopics.title: Coordinates and spatial reasoning
subtopics.teaching: Plot and interpret coordinates and reason about movement, symmetry and position.
subtopics.worked_example: The point (3,-2) is three units right and two units below the origin.
subtopics.pitfall: The first coordinate is horizontal and the second vertical.
subtopics.mastery: Use coordinate changes and symmetry to solve unfamiliar spatial problems.

subtopics.title: Arithmetic patterns
subtopics.teaching: Identify constant differences and use them to predict later terms.
subtopics.worked_example: 4,7,10,13 has constant difference 3.
subtopics.pitfall: Do not infer a rule from only one transition.
subtopics.mastery: Represent the rule by position and verify it on several terms.

subtopics.title: Geometric patterns
subtopics.teaching: Recognise constant multiplicative change and distinguish it from additive change.
subtopics.worked_example: 2,6,18,54 multiplies by 3 each time.
subtopics.pitfall: A constant ratio differs from a constant difference.
subtopics.mastery: Test the ratio across consecutive terms before generalising.

subtopics.title: Recursive rules
subtopics.teaching: Describe how each term is generated from an earlier term.
subtopics.worked_example: In 2,5,8,11 each term is the previous term plus 3.
subtopics.pitfall: A recursive rule describes progression but may not directly give the nth term.
subtopics.mastery: Trace from the initial value and verify every generated term.

subtopics.title: Visual patterns
subtopics.teaching: Translate growing diagrams into numerical relationships.
subtopics.worked_example: If each stage adds four tiles, stage totals can be modelled from that structural change.
subtopics.pitfall: Counting only an outer edge can miss repeated internal units.
subtopics.mastery: Make a stage-number table before proposing a general rule.

subtopics.title: Pattern-based reasoning
subtopics.teaching: Use patterns to discover, test and justify general relationships.
subtopics.worked_example: Test small cases to expose a possible invariant before proving it.
subtopics.pitfall: A pattern seen in three cases is evidence, not proof.
subtopics.mastery: Use algebra, parity or structural reasoning to justify the generalisation.

subtopics.title: Tables and graphs
subtopics.teaching: Read values, scales, categories and trends accurately from common data displays.
subtopics.worked_example: Always inspect the axis scale before comparing bar heights.
subtopics.pitfall: A visual gap can exaggerate a numerical difference.
subtopics.mastery: Extract exact values before calculating or drawing conclusions.

subtopics.title: Averages and spread
subtopics.teaching: Calculate and interpret mean, median, mode and range.
subtopics.worked_example: For 2,4,4,10 the mean is 5 while the median is 4.
subtopics.pitfall: Extreme values can move the mean substantially.
subtopics.mastery: Choose the statistic that matches the question and dataset.

subtopics.title: Basic probability
subtopics.teaching: Represent likelihood and calculate simple probabilities from defined sample spaces.
subtopics.worked_example: A fair die has probability 3/6=1/2 of producing an even number.
subtopics.pitfall: Probability lies from 0 to 1 inclusive.
subtopics.mastery: Define equally likely outcomes before forming the probability ratio.

subtopics.title: Counting outcomes
subtopics.teaching: Systematically count possible outcomes without omissions or duplicates.
subtopics.worked_example: Two coin tosses have HH, HT, TH and TT when order matters.
subtopics.pitfall: HT and TH are different ordered outcomes.
subtopics.mastery: Use tables, lists or tree diagrams to make the sample space explicit.

subtopics.title: Evidence from data
subtopics.teaching: Make conclusions supported by data while recognising limits.
subtopics.worked_example: A higher average does not mean every individual observation is higher.
subtopics.pitfall: A small association does not establish causation.
subtopics.mastery: State the evidence and avoid claims stronger than the dataset supports.

subtopics.title: Working backwards
subtopics.teaching: Reverse a sequence of operations to recover an unknown starting value.
subtopics.worked_example: If doubling a number and adding 7 gives 31, subtract 7 then divide by 2.
subtopics.pitfall: Reverse operations in the opposite order from the original.
subtopics.mastery: Run the original process forward to verify the recovered value.

subtopics.title: Systematic case analysis
subtopics.teaching: Break constrained problems into complete, non-overlapping cases.
subtopics.worked_example: List possible integer values under each condition rather than guessing.
subtopics.pitfall: Overlapping cases can double-count solutions.
subtopics.mastery: Define cases and show that every valid possibility is included exactly once.

subtopics.title: Invariants and constraints
subtopics.teaching: Identify properties that remain unchanged during a process.
subtopics.worked_example: A move may change token positions while preserving the total number of tokens.
subtopics.pitfall: A proposed final state violating an invariant is impossible.
subtopics.mastery: Test parity, totals, colour counts or other conserved quantities.

subtopics.title: Mathematical classification
subtopics.teaching: Classify objects using explicit mathematical properties.
subtopics.worked_example: Even and odd are complementary integer classifications, while prime and composite concern factors.
subtopics.pitfall: A visual resemblance is not a mathematical classification rule.
subtopics.mastery: State the defining property and test it consistently.

subtopics.title: Non-routine puzzles
subtopics.teaching: Combine several ideas when no standard procedure is immediately obvious.
subtopics.worked_example: Try small cases, represent the structure, identify constraints and then generalise.
subtopics.pitfall: Blind trial-and-error can miss solutions.
subtopics.mastery: Record failed approaches and use them to narrow the remaining possibilities.

subtopics.title: Translate language into mathematics
subtopics.teaching: Identify quantities, relationships, units and operations in written situations.
subtopics.worked_example: “Three times as many” represents multiplication by 3.
subtopics.pitfall: Separate essential quantities from decorative information.
subtopics.mastery: Write a short mathematical model before calculating.

subtopics.title: Rates, time and distance
subtopics.teaching: Use speed, distance and time relationships with consistent units.
subtopics.worked_example: At 60 km/h for 2.5 hours, distance is 150 km.
subtopics.pitfall: Hours and minutes must be reconciled before applying a rate.
subtopics.mastery: Check both magnitude and unit of the result.

subtopics.title: Combined work rates
subtopics.teaching: Model jointly completed tasks by adding rates rather than completion times.
subtopics.worked_example: Rates of 1/4 and 1/6 job per hour combine to 5/12 job per hour.
subtopics.pitfall: Adding completion times reverses the relationship.
subtopics.mastery: Express each worker as a fraction of one job per unit time.

subtopics.title: Multi-operation problems
subtopics.teaching: Plan sequential operations while preserving units and the meaning of intermediate quantities.
subtopics.worked_example: A shopping problem may require discount, tax and final-total calculations in a specific order.
subtopics.pitfall: Applying a percentage to the wrong base can produce a plausible number.
subtopics.mastery: Annotate each intermediate result and compare it with the story.

subtopics.title: Solution verification
subtopics.teaching: Check a word-problem answer against every stated condition.
subtopics.worked_example: A fractional number of required whole objects can signal a modelling error.
subtopics.pitfall: A correct arithmetic result can still answer the wrong question.
subtopics.mastery: Substitute the result back into the situation and verify all constraints.

subtopics.title: Efficient calculation
subtopics.teaching: Choose valid transformations that reduce calculation without sacrificing exactness.
subtopics.worked_example: 48×25 can be evaluated as 48×100÷4=1200.
subtopics.pitfall: A shortcut is useful only when its transformation preserves the value.
subtopics.mastery: Compare with an estimate or inverse operation.

subtopics.title: Estimation before exact work
subtopics.teaching: Predict the scale and reasonable range of an answer before detailed calculation.
subtopics.worked_example: 198×51 should be near 200×50, or 10,000.
subtopics.pitfall: A result far outside the estimated range is immediately suspicious.
subtopics.mastery: Use upper and lower estimates to create a reasonableness band.

subtopics.title: Answer-choice elimination
subtopics.teaching: Reject options using parity, magnitude, units and constraints.
subtopics.worked_example: If the exact answer must be even, odd choices can be eliminated with a reason.
subtopics.pitfall: Elimination is not guessing; each rejection requires evidence.
subtopics.mastery: Directly verify the remaining candidate.

subtopics.title: Error classification
subtopics.teaching: Distinguish interpretation, method, arithmetic and verification errors.
subtopics.worked_example: A copied digit error differs from choosing the wrong formula.
subtopics.pitfall: Changing only the final number may leave the misconception intact.
subtopics.mastery: Identify the first incorrect step and repair it.

subtopics.title: Timed mixed practice
subtopics.teaching: Balance speed with accuracy across unfamiliar mathematics problems.
subtopics.worked_example: Allocate time by difficulty and return to marked questions.
subtopics.pitfall: Rushing increases avoidable reading and arithmetic errors.
subtopics.mastery: Track accuracy, skipped questions and error types after each timed set.
